paragraphs: (Elyashiv the High Priest, Nehemiah, beginning of chapter 3.) Hyman finds him mentioned nowhere in halakhah or aggadah; he is mentioned only in Moed Katan 25b: when Rabbi Elyashiv died, seventy breaches were dug in Nehardea. Hyman suggests that he is the one mentioned in Bava Batra 29a, where Abaye said, “If so, those of the house of Bar Elyashiv, who object even to one who passes over their boundary”; since he was a forceful man, the thieves feared him in his lifetime. But Dikdukei Soferim’s reading in Moed Katan 25b is preferable in Hyman’s judgment: “When Rabbi Yitzchak son of Rabbi Elyashiv died, seventy breaches were dug in Tiberias.” So it is cited in the Jerusalem Talmud there: “When Rabbi Yitzchak bar Elyashiv died, seventy thresholds were uprooted from the householders of the Galilee.” There is also Rabbi Acha bar Elyashiv, Vayikra Rabbah 35:6.

notes.text: The negative corpus observation, violent-man identification, preferred Yitzchak patronymic and Nehardea/Tiberias difference are Hyman’s. The biblical parenthesis does not identify the Amora with the High Priest.

The consulted Davidson English Moed Katan 25b names Rabbi Elyashiv and Nehardea. Hyman’s preferred Dikdukei Soferim reading with Yitzchak and Tiberias remains an attributed edition claim, not independently inspected here.
